note: onChange on the weight field now enforces the previously-decorative max=2000 cap for real. Marking a set complete with weight > 2x the exercise's last recorded weight (getLastExercisePerformance) prompts an inline window.confirm ('X lb is much heavier than your last Y lb... Save it anyway?') before the set is accepted; cancel leaves the set unmarked and unsaved, accept proceeds normally. Tunable UI threshold (2x), not engine semantics -- engine-side outlier handling untouched. Known gaps, not fixed (out of scope for this finding's repro, noted for a future round): (1) the guard only runs in handleSetCompleted, so editing the weight on an already-completed set doesn't re-trigger it; (2) with no prior performance for that exercise (e.g. first-ever lift), an implausible weight like 2255 is silently clamped to 2000 with no prompt.

removeSet is now wrapped in WorkoutDetail.jsx and QuickWorkout.jsx (both use the shared useWorkoutExercises hook and ExerciseCard, so both got the fix): deleting any set shows a sonner toast ('Set N removed') with an Undo action that calls a new insertSet(exerciseIndex, setIndex, set, exerciseName) helper to reinsert the set and renumber. insertSet re-resolves the target exercise by name (falling back to a findIndex scan) and bails out to a no-op if that exercise no longer exists, since the toast's ~8s actionable lifetime is long enough for the athlete to reorder/remove/swap exercises underneath it -- prevents both a crash (undefined exercise) and silently reinserting into the wrong exercise. The toast also passes closeButton:false, since the app's global always-visible close button (App.jsx) is pinned top-right and otherwise overlaps/intercepts the Undo tap target in the mobile bottom-center toast position.
